input: In this work, a comparison is presented between two forms of a copper-zinc oxide catalyst for the reaction of carbon dioxide and hydrogen to give methanol, the purpose being to establish how the form of the catalyst affects the performance that is obtained. The basis of the comparison is the space-time yield, which is defined as the mass of product formed per unit volume of catalyst per hour (kg L-1 h-1). Both catalysts were tested under one and the same set of conditions, namely a temperature of 250 °C, a pressure of 50 bar, a feed ratio H2/CO2 = 3 and a single feed composition, so that the differences that were observed may be attributed to the form of the catalyst rather than to any difference in the conditions applied. The structured catalyst gave a space-time yield of 0.68 kg L-1 h-1, accompanied by a pressure drop of 0.22 bar and an activity loss of 7% after 100 h of operation. The pellet catalyst, by contrast, gave a space-time yield of 0.45 kg L-1 h-1, with a considerably higher pressure drop of 0.99 bar and an activity loss of 15% after 100 h. Taken together, these results indicate that, under the conditions examined, the structured form produced more methanol per unit volume of catalyst, whilst at the same time imposing a lower pressure drop on the feed and losing less of its activity over the period of the test. It should be noted, however, that the comparison has been carried out at one feed composition and at one set of conditions only, and the ranking that emerges is a ranking at those conditions. It should also be noted that no sulfur-bearing feed was tested in the course of the work, and that yield and pressure drop are seldom reported for one and the same catalyst charge, while the activity losses that are reported relate to the position at the end of the test period, so that the behaviour of the catalysts beyond that period remains unreported.
target: Carbon dioxide and hydrogen react over a copper-zinc oxide catalyst to give methanol, and the form of the catalyst changes the performance the reaction gives. Space-time yield, the mass of product per unit catalyst volume per hour (kg L-1 h-1), was measured for a structured catalyst and a pellet catalyst under the same conditions: 250 °C, 50 bar, a feed ratio H2/CO2 = 3, and one feed composition. The structured catalyst gave a space-time yield of 0.68 kg L-1 h-1, a pressure drop of 0.22 bar, and an activity loss of 7% after 100 h. The pellet catalyst gave a space-time yield of 0.45 kg L-1 h-1, a pressure drop of 0.99 bar, and an activity loss of 15% after 100 h. The two catalysts were tested on the same reaction, the same feed and the same charge basis, so the differences recorded are differences of catalyst form. Pressure drop is the cost of passing the feed through the bed, and on that measure the pellet bed is the more expensive passage for the lower yield. The structured form produced more methanol per unit volume, at the lower pressure drop, and lost less activity over the test period. The ranking is a ranking at the stated conditions: the yield difference is a difference in the rate per unit volume, not in the equilibrium the reaction can reach, and a different feed composition or temperature could change the gap between the forms. The results support the structured form for this reaction at the tested conditions. No sulfur-bearing feed was tested, so the comparison does not extend to feeds that carry sulfur. Yield and pressure drop are seldom reported for the same catalyst charge, and the activity losses are the losses at the end of the test period; behaviour beyond that period is not reported.
